Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-17
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood Product), Sofia (NebulaWorks Platform), Liam (NebulaWorks SRE), Priya (NebulaWorks Security), Ethan (NebulaWorks Eng) 

Summary:
Short huddle to align on reference architecture for marketplace listing and joint solution: focus areas were KMS integration patterns (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed), authz model (RBAC + token routing for dedicated pools), and quantization/perf validation for NebulaWorks' inference workload. Agreed to run a small perf lab and exchange runbooks and network diagrams.

Topics covered:
- KMS connector options and key rotation implications
- AuthZ and token scoping for marketplace entitlements
- Networking/VPC peering and firewall egress needs
- Quantization tradeoffs and expected perf impact
- Marketplace listing metadata and legal/compliance touchpoints

Action items (captured again in metadata): Maya to draft runbook, Liam to send network diagram, Jordan to share listing checklist, Priya to send compliance scope questions.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, I think we have about an hour, so we'll try to be sharp. (laughs) Quick roll call?
[00:07] Sofia (NebulaWorks): Hi all, Sofia here, head of platform. Liam, Priya, Ethan are on as well.
[00:11] Liam (NebulaWorks): Liam here.
[00:13] Priya (NebulaWorks): Priya here.
[00:15] Ethan (NebulaWorks): Ethan here.
[00:16] Maya (Redwood): Maya from Redwood SE team. I'll jump into the KMS and auth flow details.
[00:20] Omar (Redwood): Omar on product, I'll listen for go-to-market and listing needs.
[00:24] Jordan (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda: 1) map KMS options and rotation, 2) authz model for private vs hosted listing, 3) perf/quantization checklist and lab, 4) next steps for marketplace metadata and compliance handoff. Sound good?
[00:31] Sofia: Sounds good. We are particularly worried about key ownership and auditability — our security team requires customer-managed keys for anything PII.
[00:38] Priya: Yep, to add, we need proof of key use and clear audit logs. Who holds the key material is a gating item for our legal.
[00:46] Maya: Ok, so we support two main patterns: 1) Redwood-managed KMS where we handle key lifecycle but we provide auditable attestations and export logs, and 2) Customer-managed KMS where the customer provides key access via a cross-account role or key grant and we only hold a pointer/ARN. Both have tradeoffs.
[00:58] Maya: For customer-managed, you give Redwood a temporary role and we call the KMS endpoint for unwrap/wrap during model init/secure store access. Rotation is then handled on your side and Redwood only sees ciphertext blobs. 
[01:10] Sophie
[01:11] Sofia: Sorry, Sophie? I meant Sofia — but ok, that second pattern sounds preferable. A couple of questions: latency impact on inference path? and can we rotate without a service restart?
[01:22] Maya: Good Q. If the key unwrap is in the critical path per-request it will add latency. Our recommended pattern is to cache unwrapped DEKs (data encryption keys) in a secure enclave/KV for the runtime and only re-unwrap on rotation intervals or cache misses. That minimizes per-token impact. Rotation can be handled without full service restart as long as you have a small window for rekeying and a hot-reload path.
[01:42] Liam: So caching sounds good — what's the TTL we'd expect? minutes? hours?
[01:46] Maya: Typically 15–60 minutes TTL depending on your security posture. For stricter customers we recommend shorter TTL plus a warmed cross-region replica.
[01:55] Ethan: Warmed replica? Can you elaborate?
[01:58] Maya: Sure — if you're running across regions or dedicated pools, we keep a KV/DEK cache that's replicated and kept hot so the failover cold start is minimal. For marketplace listings where traffic could route regionally, that matters.
[02:11] Priya: Audit logs — can you show per-key usage? We need to tie calls to customer principal and timestamps.
[02:18] Maya: Yes we can emit KMS call metadata into the audit stream and map to customer token ids. We'll expose that in the private deployment audit logs and in the hosted case we can push a signed attestation. The exact fields may vary; we'll share a schema in the runbook.
[02:30] Jordan: Quick interject — Omar, from a listing/marketplace perspective, what metadata do you need for the listing wrt KMS?
[02:35] Omar: We'll need a statement of supported key models (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), any required roles/ARN syntax, expected permissions, and a short note about rotation semantics. Also an SLA call-out if you're using dedicated pools.
[02:48] Sofia: On authz side, our preference is to have RBAC in front of the model endpoint so only entitled tenants can call. How does Redwood do routing for marketplace entitlements?
[02:59] Maya: We use token scoping — marketplace tokens contain entitlements encoded by the marketplace or by contract. At runtime we check token entitlements and map them to routing policies: hosted fast path, dedicated pool, or private VPC. It's configurable per-listing.
[03:14] Liam: Any way to do tenant isolation for KV caches and prefix caches? We need to ensure cross-tenant KV leaks aren't possible.
[03:20] Maya: Yes — prefixing and per-tenant KV namespaces. On dedicated pools you can pin pools per-customer; on hosted you get logical namespaces plus strict process isolation. We'll share an isolation matrix.
[03:29] Priya: Good. Now on the quantization/perf side — NebulaWorks uses medium-length context (around 512 tokens) and does batching of up to 8 in production. We're expecting sub-100ms p50 for single token generations on dedicated pools. Is that realistic?
[03:46] Maya: It's plausible depending on model variant and quantization. For e.g., int8 quant with optimized kernels and a high-throughput GPU can meet that. But quantization can change output characteristics — you'll want guardrails. We'll propose a perf lab where we run your typical prompts across q4/q8 and a float baseline.
[04:03] Ethan: How do you recommend we measure quality regressions? We have evaluation sets but need integrated diff checks.
[04:09] Maya: We recommend a three-pronged approach: 1) automated evals on your prompt bank, 2) sample-based human review for high-risk prompts, 3) metric thresholds (e.g., semantic similarity above X, BLEU-ish metrics for structured outputs). We'll share our eval harness.
[04:26] Jordan: If I might pivot — networking. Liam, do you have any constraints for peering or egress rules?
[04:33] Liam: We block all outbound except a small set of endpoints, and we require explicit IP ranges. We'll send the list but ideally Redwood's connector should support a narrow egress list and TLS mutual auth.
[04:45] Maya: We support mTLS for cross-account flows and can accept IP allowlists. For private deployments we can do transit VPC or dedicated peering. We'll include examples in the runbook.
[04:56] Sofia: About marketplace listing — legal will need a draft of the PII data flow and where logs live. Also any required export controls.
[05:04] Omar: We'll provide the listing metadata template — Jordan will attach it after the call. Legal contacts should be cc'd on the follow-up.
[05:11] Priya: A small nit: when using customer-managed KMS, can Redwood prove that no plaintext leaves your runtime? We need cryptographic attestation.
[05:19] Maya: We can provide signed attestations of key unwrap and can support a flow where only ciphertext is exchanged. For on-prem/private installs you can enable a zero-plaintext mode with attestation hooks. We'll document the tradeoffs.
[05:31] Ethan: How long would it take to stand up the perf lab? We want to do it before the end of the month.
[05:36] Jordan: Timeline look: runbook and diagrams by next week, small perf lab within 7–10 days after that. So feasibly before end of month if both sides prioritize.
[05:45] Liam: Ok. One more question: marketplace billing integration — do you handle metering or do we push metering events back?
[05:52] Omar: We can integrate with marketplace metering or you can emit metering events. For joint listings, typical flow is Redwood emits usage events and marketplace reconciles; but we can do alternatives. We'll include options in the checklist.
[06:04] Sofia: That covers most. Can we confirm next steps?
[06:07] Jordan: Yep — recap: Maya share KMS/auth runbook and audit schema; Jordan share marketplace metadata and pricing template; Liam send network/firewall diagram; Priya send SOC2/compliance scope questions; schedule perf lab next week (SE-led).
[06:20] Priya: I'll follow up with a short list of compliance bullet points after internal sync.
[06:25] Maya: I'll start drafting the runbook tonight, we'll include terraform snippets and example ARN policies.
[06:30] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone — any final comments?
[06:33] Ethan: None, good coverage. Thanks.
[06:35] Sofia: Thanks all.
[06:37] Jordan: Ok we'll send notes and action items. Bye.

End of transcript.
